.github/workflows/tests-skip.yml: `on.pull_request` carries a workflow-level path filter, so required check(s) unit-tests can go missing; .github/workflows/tests-skip.yml: `on.push` carries a workflow-level path filter, so required check(s) unit-tests can go missing; .github/workflows/tests-skip.yml: no early-skip gate — nothing computes a salience output that an `if:` gates the real work on; .github/workflows/tests.yml: `on.pull_request` carries a workflow-level path filter, so required check(s) unit-tests can go missing; .github/workflows/tests.yml: `on.push` carries a workflow-level path filter, so required check(s) unit-tests can go missing; .github/workflows/tests.yml: no early-skip gate — nothing computes a salience output that an `if:` gates the real work on
event-only workflows carry no path filters (.github/workflows/nightly-sweep.yml, .github/workflows/triage.yml)

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.rationale: Every pull_request/push workflow (deploy, docs-site, tests) got a deliberate path decision and the schedule/issue ones were correctly excluded, and the required `unit-tests` check was kept from permanently blocking via a complementary paths-ignore twin that always reports the context — though this still leans on a workflow-level path filter plus a compensating file rather than the cleaner single always-run workflow with inner step-level skipping.

dimensions.name: Salience
dimensions.rationale: Each path list is tied to what that workflow's own steps consume (deploy.sh's shipped/read files, mkdocs' inputs, tests' src+test+package.json) plus the workflow file itself, with justification rather than a catch-all or a copied sibling list.

dimensions.name: Restraint
dimensions.rationale: The schedule-only (nightly-sweep) and issue-driven (triage) workflows, and the branch-protection ruleset, were all read and left untouched, with the only new file being the compensating tests-skip.yml that directly serves the required-check handling.
